trigger: blinded — the hero's Blind lands on a foe
before: Viper cannot see a thing for 1 round: it hits only on its die's top face.
after: Viper cannot see a thing for the rest of the fight: it hits only on its die's top face and never lands a critical.
why: Blind is now blindness for the fight at every depth (the three-round timer past floor 12 is gone) and a blind foe never lands a critical, so the line says both and drops the rounds.

trigger: blinded — the hero's Blind lands on a foe
before: Viper is blind for 3 rounds: it hits only on its top face.
after: Viper is blind for the fight: it hits only on its top face and never crits.
why: The rail twin: for the fight, top face only, never a critical; no rounds.

trigger: petrified — the hero's Petrify lands on a foe
after: Viper turns to stone and does not get back up. A statue carries no spoils.
why: Petrify now kills (experience paid by the kill line after it, Q2 A), so the line says the foe does not get back up, and that a statue drops nothing.

trigger: petrified — the hero's Petrify lands on a foe
after: Viper turns to stone and dies. No spoils from a statue.
why: The rail twin: stone, dead, no spoils.

trigger: stupefied — the hero's Stupidity lands on a foe
before: Viper forgets what it is doing, for the rest of the fight.
after: Viper forgets most of what it knew: its intelligence is down to 1 for the rest of the fight. It still swings, but it resists almost nothing now.
why: Stupidity now drops the foe's intelligence to 1 for the fight and the foe keeps swinging, so the line names the intelligence it had (the event's `was`), the 1 it has, and that it still swings; the frozen voice variants carry no `was`, so the corpus reads the plain form.

trigger: stupefied — the hero's Stupidity lands on a foe
before: Viper forgets what it is doing, for the fight.
after: Viper forgets most of it: intelligence down to 1 for the fight.
why: The rail twin: the intelligence it dropped to, for the fight.

trigger: foeStupefied — removed: a stupid foe no longer skips its turns (engine/combat.js#foeTurn)
before: Viper stands there, thinking about nothing.
why: Stupidity no longer skips the foe's turns, so "stands there, thinking about nothing" would be false and the event is not emitted any more.

trigger: foeStupefied — removed: a stupid foe no longer skips its turns
before: Viper stands there, thinking about nothing.
why: The rail twin of the removed per-turn skip line.

trigger: the out-of-combat rail family title for foeStupefied (removed with the event)
why: The foeStupefied event is gone, so its rail family title goes with it.

trigger: a foe condition's line on the long-press foe card
before: It hits only on its die's top face until it can see again: the count on the chip, or the whole fight if there is none. It is swinging at where you were a moment ago.
after: It hits only on its die's top face and never lands a critical, until it can see again: the count on the chip, or the whole fight if there is none. It is swinging at where you were a moment ago.
why: A blind foe also never lands a critical now, so the card says so beside the top-face cap.

trigger: a foe condition's line on the long-press foe card
before: It does nothing at all for the rest of the fight, and it is easier to hit. Nobody is home.
after: Its intelligence is down to 1 for the rest of the fight, so it shrugs off almost nothing you cast on it. It is still swinging, which is the worrying part.
why: A stupid foe is no longer skipped or easier to hit: its intelligence is 1 for the fight and it keeps swinging, so the old "does nothing at all" line was false.

trigger: a foe condition chip label (removed: no Stone hold exists)
why: Petrify kills instead of holding, so the reserved Stone chip label is never shown.

trigger: a foe condition's line on the long-press foe card (removed: no Stone hold exists)
before: Turned to stone. As conditions go, this one is fairly permanent.
why: Petrify kills instead of holding, so the reserved Stone description is never shown.

trigger: a spell's Grimoire and scroll text
before: control · one foe · does nothing at all for the rest of the fight; past floor 12, only for three rounds
after: control · one foe · its intelligence drops to 1 for the fight, so it resists almost nothing (a 20 on a d20, a little more as you go deeper), and it keeps swinging
why: Stupidity drops the foe's intelligence to 1 for the fight (so it resists almost nothing) and the foe keeps swinging; the floor-12 three-round clause is gone with the cap.

trigger: a spell's Grimoire and scroll text
before: control · one foe · blind for life, which in here means the fight; past floor 12, life lasts three rounds
after: control · one foe · blind for the fight: it hits only on its die's top face and never lands a critical
why: Blind lasts the fight at every depth, hits only on the die's top face and never crits; the floor-12 three-round clause is gone.

trigger: a spell's Grimoire and scroll text
before: control · one foe · stone for five days; no spoils; past floor 12, five days shrink to three rounds
after: control · one foe · turns to stone and dies; you get the experience and none of the spoils, because statues carry nothing
why: Petrify turns the foe to stone and it dies (Q2 A: you get the experience, no spoils); "five days" and the floor-12 three-round clause are gone.
